note: Adapted from the new-species description in Hill (1942), original in English. Measurements in mm; the soldier measurements are given in the original in two columns (Tamworth / Griffith) and are transcribed here as two sets of values. Distribution: Victoria, near Swan Hill (type locality), Redcliffs, Halbert, Violet Town, Charlton, Linga; New South Wales, near Griffith, Pillaga, Dubbo, Tamworth, near Wagga Wagga, Broken Hill; Western Australia, Kalgoorlie. The type material is a soldier holotype in the C.S.I.R. collection. The original states explicitly that the alate measurements come only from the Wagga Wagga series that "may belong to this species", so neither the alate description nor its measurements are confirmed. OCR problem: "lon S" in the soldier measurement table is a misrecognition of "long".

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The original states that authentic examples of this caste are not known; only a series from Wagga Wagga containing soldiers and workers may belong to this species, and that series differs from M. leai in its measurements only. Measurements (mm, from that doubtful series): length with wings 6.30—7.25; length without wings 4.25—5.25; head length (to apex of labrum) 0.88—0.91; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.51—0.55; head width 0.77—0.80; greatest diameter of compound eye 0.22; ocellus length 0.07; pronotum length 0.36; pronotum width 0.58; fore wing length 5.00—5.45; fore wing width 1.36.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Closely related to M. boreus and M. leai; smaller than the former with finer mandibles, larger than the latter with stouter mandibles; it differs from both in the fairly distinct, slightly square depression on the frons (Fig. 351). Measurements (mm; the original gives two columns, Tamworth / Griffith): body length 4.75 / 5.40—6.10; head length including mandibles 2.49 / 2.60—2.78; head length (to clypeal suture) 1.39 / 1.43—1.54; head width 0.84 / 0.84—0.86; pronotum length 0.27 / 0.29; pronotum width 0.55 / 0.60—0.62.
